It is strange to me that the instance of Abelian (Rep k G) in Rep.Iso requires that k is commutative. I don't think mathematically we need the coefficient ring k to be commutative to obtain the equivalence between k[G]-mod and G-Rep_k, right? If k is not commutative, then neither k[G] or End_k(V) is a k-algebra (a k-algebra R means a ring map k->R with image lying in the center of R; the G action is k-linear but the k action may not be k-linear) and the expression k[G]\->_a[k] V \-> _l[k] V is broken. But we still have a ring map from k[G] to End_add(V), so we get a k[G]-module anyway. Conversely, since G commutes with k in k[G], the G action on a k[G] module is k-linear so it gives a k-representation of G. Why do we choose the 'MonoidAlgebra.lift' approach?

I noticed that there is a comment in Rep.Iso
-- TODO Verify that the equivalence with `ModuleCat k[G]` is a monoidal functor.
The monoidal structure does require k to be commutative, but right now all we have in Rep.Iso is an equivalence of categories which mathematically has nothing to do with the commutativity of k.

I opened a PR #41616 to remove the commutativity assumption. It is an one line instance in Rep.Basic right after the discussion of RepIsoAction. I am not sure if we should remove the instance abelian (Rep k G) in Rep.Iso where the commutativity is assumed.
